### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/trigger-record-change`, touching **6** documentable anchor(s).

**6** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`  _(via SchemaRegistry (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/deployment/environment-variables.mdx`  _(via SchemaRegistry (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/kernel/services-checklist.mdx`  _(via SchemaRegistry (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via handlePackagesRequest (symbol, a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/plugins/adding-a-metadata-type.mdx`  _(via SchemaRegistry (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/plugin-spec.mdx`  _(via SchemaRegistry (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-4.mdx`  _(via SchemaRegistry (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **59** of **211** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **37** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 91e46522c171a319825aa9a43626472c065c29d0` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `6892b2d68917860c686bd8f94eabda129c6e6973` — the merge of head `c403c6bd5a7a21179eded7d5741e16f9ac87a80d` into base `91e46522c171a319825aa9a43626472c065c29d0`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 6892b2d68917860c686bd8f94eabda129c6e6973 && git checkout 6892b2d68917860c686bd8f94eabda129c6e6973
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 91e46522c171a319825aa9a43626472c065c29d0 c403c6bd5a7a21179eded7d5741e16f9ac87a80d && git checkout -B drift-repro 91e46522c171a319825aa9a43626472c065c29d0 && git merge --no-ff c403c6bd5a7a21179eded7d5741e16f9ac87a80d

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 91e46522c171a319825aa9a43626472c065c29d0
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 91e46522c171a319825aa9a43626472c065c29d0` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `c403c6bd5a7a21179eded7d5741e16f9ac87a80d`
Local-runs: none

Face: the declaration face only (`Clause-②: yes (widening)` on the PR body and on `.changeset/28117-disable-app-module.md`). The committed tree touches no `packages/spec/src/**` and no governed path, so this review has no ④. Read against card #28117 (body items 1–5), scope addendum 6523684730, the dispatch order, and the dev report 6538834934. Inputs: `git diff origin/main...c403c6bd` and the cited code on the head tree (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/package-writability.ts`, `SchemaRegistry.isPackageDisabled` / `isObjectPackageDisabled`, `ObjectQLEngine` nav-contribution registration, the marketplace install's `register(…, { source: 'marketplace' })`).

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The widened accept set matches the ruling. Correct.** `PATCH /api/v1/packages/:id/disable` reads `isDisableableAppModule(qlService, id)` before `requireWritablePackage`. That accepts a package only when all three hold:
   - the row's `manifest.type === 'module'`;
   - its own `manifest.scope` is not in `READ_ONLY_PACKAGE_SCOPES` (`system`, `cloud`), and the predicate imports that constant rather than spelling it again;
   - `declaredDependencyIds(manifest)` DIRECTLY names a package other than itself whose registry row says `manifest.type === 'app'`.

   This is card item 1: a module that belongs to an installed app, with a tie the registry measurably carries on both install paths. The artifact package list is not persisted, the declared dependency is, and the namespace follows from it. The order sits after `requireManageMetadata`, the catalog wall and the query refusal, so none of those changed. A request outside that set still answers `422 WRITABLE_PACKAGE_REQUIRED` exactly as before. That covers the app, plugins, drivers, platform packages, a module of a plugin, an orphan module, a module whose app is absent, and a `system`-scoped module of the app. The test pins seven of these cases on both install paths. An unknown id still falls through to the existing 404.
2. **Authoring is still refused, and `isWritablePackage` is unchanged. Correct.** `packages/metadata-protocol` is not in the diff. `isDisableableAppModule` has exactly one call site (the disable door, L1789). The doors at L1571 (install/overwrite), L1820 (publish), L2336 (revert), L2376 (adopt), L2502 (edit) and L2603 (delete) still ask `requireWritablePackage` alone, and `withWritableVerdict` (L832) still serves `writable: isWritablePackage(…)`, which is `false` for a module. Edit, publish and delete are pinned 422 in the test. Revert, adopt and overwrite are not pinned, but they go through the same unchanged call (read, not measured). `writable` is not overloaded (card item 4).
3. **REST answer codes. Correct.** A disable answers 200 with the row (`enabled: false`) and an enable answers 200. While the module is disabled, its objects answer `404 OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED` (the existing refusal, now pinned on the module path), and the app's own object still answers 200. No code is new and no code is renamed.
4. **The nav fold. Correct and consistent with the one meaning.** `applyNavContributions` skips `c.packageId` when `isPackageDisabled` is true, before the group lookup, so the module's items are not folded, not relocated and not diagnosed. Every reader goes through this one fold: `getApp`, `getAllApps`, and the protocol's `app` list and by-name reads. The stored app is not mutated, and the state is asked per read, so an enable restores the items with nothing to invalidate. Contributions are registered only through `ObjectQLEngine`'s manifest registration (engine.ts L8842), and before this PR the door refused every such package. So no package that the public door could disable loses menu items it showed before. This is not a narrowing.
5. **Record-change withholding. Correct and consistent.** `RecordChangeTrigger` returns before dispatch when `engine.registry.isObjectPackageDisabled(binding.object ?? ctx.object)` is true. That is the owner question the data plane's refusal asks, so an overlay from a disabled package does not take the object offline. The write itself is untouched, so the data is kept, and the check runs per write, so an enable resumes the flow. The base was measured red (an in-process write fired the flow) and is green at head, the ablation bites, and the real-kernel test proves the production engine carries `registry`. The rule applies to every disabled package, not only modules. That is what card item 3 orders ("a disabled package's objects"). No request is newly refused, so this is not an accept-set narrowing, and the PR's "Nothing is narrowed" stands.
6. **Handbook (`content/docs/deployment/marketplace-handbook.mdx`). Consistent.** Step 7 no longer says every code- or app-provided package answers the disable door 422, which would now be false. It names the module exemption. The new "Disabling a module" section states the one meaning (data plane, navigation, flows, restart, authoring), and every claim matches the code above. It also states plainly what the addendum asked to be measured: an app hook's `ctx.api.object()` is served the kept rows, with no `OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED` to catch in-process.
7. **Undeclared widening: none found.**
   - The only new accept is the declared one.
   - `RecordChangeDataEngine` (exported from `@objectstack/trigger-record-change`) gains an optional structural `registry?` member. That is an additive, non-breaking type change: implementers need nothing new, and an engine without the member dispatches as before. It falls under the PR's `yes (widening)` declaration, though the changeset text does not name it (non-blocking).
   - No spec, served key, error code or manifest key moves, so `Metadata-protocol: none` is right.

Non-blocking notes (no must-fix):
- (a) The scope exemption reads the MODULE's own scope only. An unscoped module that declares a `system`-scoped app (for example `setup`) would qualify. No in-tree `type: 'module'` package does this today: every platform-shipped package carries `scope: 'system'` itself. The ruling's "platform packages keep 422" holds for every package that exists now. If a platform app ever ships unscoped modules, this is the line to revisit.
- (b) The handbook does not yet say what the PR's Acceptance notes do. A disabled module's own code hooks still run on in-process writes to its objects, and its record-change flows bound to an ENABLED package's object still fire. Both are outside card item 3 as written, and both belong to the open decision below. They are worth one sentence in the handbook once that decision is made.

### ② Semver level

`patch` for `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/objectql` and `@objectstack/trigger-record-change`. These are exactly the three published packages whose source the diff moves; the handbook is prose, not a package. AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3 says `Metadata-protocol: none` takes `patch`, and that a non-protocol widening ships `patch`. Both declaration lines are line-initial in the PR body and in the changeset body, and the `Clause-②: yes (widening)` arm is well-formed. Correct.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **open_questions[0], `status: needs_decision`. Not settled by this PR, and not ruled here.** An app hook's in-process `ctx.api.object(name)` read or write of a DISABLED module's object is served, as measured and pinned. Only the data plane and the by-name reads refuse with `404 OBJECT_PACKAGE_DISABLED`. That differs from what addendum 6523684730 item 1 expected app code to meet. The PR does not soften any answer, because it adds no fallback or empty result and the in-process path was never refused. So it keeps addendum item 1's "do not soften" line and fully delivers item 2 (measure, pin, document). Whether to refuse the in-process path (the dev's options A/B/C) is the maintainer's decision, raised to the seat. If that decision is routed onto #28117 rather than a new card, `Fixes #28117` must become `Part of #28117` before landing, as the dev report says.
- **out_of_scope_findings[0], the served-verdict Seam (card item 4).** `spec:SERVED_ROW_VERDICTS → runtime:withWritableVerdict | renderer:PackagesPage.tsx L1054` is reported, not written, as the order requires. Until that key ships, the Console cannot offer Disable for these rows. The server door accepts it, and the Console card is `Blocked-by` this one. The seat carries it.
- **Card item 6** (the ADR-0070 D2 addendum line) is routed to #28285. `docs/adr/**` is untouched, so this PR stays Tier S.
- **Author.** The PR's `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, so no extra login is named.
- **CI at this head.** At read time, no check run had failed, and several (Test Core shards, Build Core, Type Check workspace/consumer/debt, Live E2E UI, Lint repo & tooling) were still in progress. CI is the landing check's half, not this record's.
